extracted.intended_audience: serious fiction and narrative nonfiction/memoir writers applying to a summer writers' workshop
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and expectations for writers seeking admission to the Squaw Valley Community of Writers summer workshop, including what manuscripts are eligible, how submissions are evaluated, and what participants can expect from the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions based on manuscript merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions are based on the merit of submitted manuscripts alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is determined solely by the quality of the submitted work (not by recommendations, resume, or other factors). Financial aid is available; tuition is $995. Note that tuition does not include housing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction/memoir eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonfiction or memoir submissions should be in a narrative form; travel, self-help, how-to, and scholarly works will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only narrative-style nonfiction/memoir is acceptable for admission and workshop critique. Explicitly excluded genres: travel writing, self-help, instructional/how-to texts, and scholarly/academic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary workshop manuscript requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants bring a workshop manuscript that will be critiqued in daily morning workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each participant must submit a main manuscript for the morning workshop; expect detailed, recurring critique from staff writers, editors, or agents across the week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second manuscript allowed for individual conference
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to their workshop manuscript, participants may have a second manuscript read by a staff member who meets with them in an individual conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants may submit a second piece for one-on-one feedback during an individual conference — this is separate from the morning workshop manuscript and provides additional personalized critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate genre-specific morning workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: There are separate morning workshops for Fiction and Narrative Nonfiction/Memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit to the appropriate track (fiction vs. narrative nonfiction/memoir); workshop feedback and expectations will be tailored to the chosen genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop staffing and critique leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: The morning workshops are led by staff writer-teachers, editors, or agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect workshop leadership from a mix of professional writers, editors, and literary agents; this affects the perspective and types of feedback given (craft, editing, publication-oriented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program components and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The week offers daily morning workshops, craft lectures, panel discussions on editing and publishing, staff readings, and brief individual conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should be prepared for a full schedule: workshop critiques in the mornings and additional instructional/publishing-oriented events in afternoons/evenings (craft talks, panels, readings). The program includes specialty offerings such as the Finding the Story Workshop and an Open Workshop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity and participant environment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workshop is cohort-based with roughly 124 participants, so applicants should expect a communal environment and mix of peer feedback in addition to staff critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial and housing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition is $995, which includes six evening meals. Tuition does not include housing costs. Housing provided ranges from $275 - $800 for the week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission implies a financial commitment beyond application; applicants should budget for tuition plus separate housing fees. Financial aid is available and applicants may inquire about support.
